questions.question: The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. For a real $3\times5$ matrix $A$, of which space is $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ a subspace?
options: $\mathbb{R}^8$, since it combines rows and columns

questions.question: The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. A sequence of elementary row operations turns $A$ into its echelon form $R$. Which of these subspaces is guaranteed to be the same for $A$ and $R$?
options: The row space, but not in general the column space
Only the column space, as row operations mix columns
Both the row space and the column space
Neither; only the rank is preserved

questions.question: The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. $A$ has been reduced to a row echelon form $R$. Which set is a basis of $\operatorname{Row}(A)$?
options: The pivot columns of the original $A$
Those columns of $R$ that contain pivots

questions.question: The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. For a real $4\times7$ matrix $A$, how does $\dim \operatorname{Row}(A)$ compare with $\dim \operatorname{Col}(A)$, the dimension of the column space?
options: They are $7$ and $4$, the numbers of columns and rows
They are equal only when $A$ is square
The row space is larger, as rows are longer

questions.question: Each row of $A$ is the coefficient vector of one equation of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$. What does a vector in the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$, the span of the rows, represent?
options: A vector $\boldsymbol{x}$ that satisfies every equation of $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$
Coefficients of a linear combination of the equations
A right-hand side $\boldsymbol{b}$ for which the system is solvable
A direction in which solutions of the system can move freely

questions.question: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0&1\\2&4&1&3\\3&6&1&4\end{pmatrix}$, whose reduced row echelon form has nonzero rows $(1,2,0,1)$ and $(0,0,1,1)$. Every vector of the row space has the form $a(1,2,0,1)+b(0,0,1,1)$. Which vector lies in the row space?
Which set is a basis of the row space of $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&2\\2&2&5\end{pmatrix}$?
The system $x_1+2x_2=4$, $x_2-x_3=1$ has coefficient rows $(1,2,0)$ and $(0,1,-1)$. Which equation follows from it by combining its equations?
Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Which vector is orthogonal to every vector of the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$?

The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. Why does an elementary row operation, such as replacing row $2$ by row $2$ minus $3$ times row $1$, leave the row space unchanged?
options: Because it changes no individual row of $A$
New rows combine old rows, and the step can be undone
Because it leaves the rank of $A$ unchanged
Because it leaves the columns of $A$ unchanged

questions.question: The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. Why are the nonzero rows of a row echelon form $R$ linearly independent?
options: Because row operations make the rows orthogonal
Because every nonzero vector is linearly independent
Because there are at most as many of them as columns
Below each leading entry, all lower rows have zeros

questions.question: The row space of a real matrix $M$ is $\operatorname{Row}(M)$, the span of the rows of $M$. For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&1&-1\end{pmatrix}$, which set is a basis of the row space of $A^{\top}$?

The row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ of a real matrix $A$ is the span of its rows. A real $3\times5$ matrix $A$ has $\operatorname{rank}A=2$. What are $\dim\operatorname{Row}(A)$ and $\dim\operatorname{Null}(A)$?
Let $A$ be a real $m\times n$ matrix. Which set equals its row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$, the span of the rows?

A real $4\times4$ matrix has rows $\boldsymbol{r}_1=(1,0,2,1)$, $\boldsymbol{r}_2=(0,1,1,3)$, $\boldsymbol{r}_3=\boldsymbol{r}_1+\boldsymbol{r}_2$ and $\boldsymbol{r}_4=2\boldsymbol{r}_1-\boldsymbol{r}_2$. What is the dimension of its row space?
For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, with row space $\operatorname{span}\{(1,0)\}$, which operation on $A$ can change the row space?
For a real square matrix $A$, how is "$A$ is symmetric" related to "the row space $\operatorname{Row}(A)$ equals the column space $\operatorname{Col}(A)$"?
options: Symmetric is sufficient but not necessary
Every matrix with equal row and column space is symmetric
Symmetric is neither necessary nor sufficient

questions.question: Let $B$ be $k\times m$ and $A$ be $m\times n$, both real. How is the row space of $BA$ related to the row space of $A$?
options: It contains it, since $BA$ can have more rows than $A$
They are always equal, since $B$ only acts on the rows
It is contained in it, since each row of $BA$ combines rows of $A$
They are unrelated, since they lie in different spaces

questions.question: For $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0&1\\2&4&1&3\\3&6&1&4\end{pmatrix}$, whose reduced row echelon form has nonzero rows $(1,2,0,1)$ and $(0,0,1,1)$, row $3$ of $A$ equals row $1$ plus row $2$. For which right-hand sides $\boldsymbol{b}=(b_1,b_2,b_3)^{\top}$ is $A\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ consistent?
For which real $k$ does $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&1\\2&k&2\\1&2&1\end{pmatrix}$ have a one-dimensional row space?
options: No $k$: three nonzero rows span at least two dimensions
